text:
anna-accounting: Uploaded invoice from BrightTree Consulting — looks like a remote contractor. Invoice attached (invoice_2026-03-15_BT.pdf). Net: £8,000, VAT: £0.00, total: £8,000. Vendor note: 'outside scope / reverse charge may apply'. They included VAT# EE123456789. Can finance confirm VAT handling and whether we need to gross-up? cc @maria-fin

vendor-billing-bot: Invoice uploaded: invoice_2026-03-15_BT.pdf (file id: inv_78923)

maria-fin: Thanks Anna. Do we have vendor country and legal entity? Also: did they send any tax certificate (VAT/VIES screenshot or W-8/W-9)? If they are EU-registered we need validation for our records.

tom-sales: They were contracted by our product team for a 6-week engagement. Mostly remote, but vendor rep mentioned two onsite days in London in Feb — unclear if that changes place-of-supply.

oliver-legal: Quick note: place-of-supply rules determine VAT treatment; if supplier is non-UK and supplies services to a UK business, reverse charge often applies and the recipient accounts for VAT. We need: supplier country, supplier VAT reg doc (or VIES validation), and the invoice wording showing reverse charge or no VAT. If they claim US W-8, that's for US withholding only (different).

anna-accounting: Copying invoice snippet below:
```
Supplier: BrightTree Consulting
Supplier country: Estonia
Invoice date: 2026-03-15
Description: Consulting services (platform integration)
Amount (net GBP): 8000.00
VAT: 0.00  (note on invoice: "reverse charge may apply")
Supplier VAT: EE123456789
```

maria-fin: OK — Estonia supplier. Please ask vendor for a VIES validation screenshot for EE123456789 and a reissued invoice that either: (a) includes their VAT number and a statement "VAT reverse charge - customer to account for VAT" or (b) if they insist no VAT, provide their VAT registration certificate and a short explanation.

liam-ops: For AP processing, should we code this as tax_code: REVERSE_CHARGE_EU? Our payment reconciliations need the tax treatment flagged so GL is correct.

oliver-legal: Yes @liam-ops, tag as reverse charge if they provide the VIES proof and the invoice references the reverse charge mechanism. If they cannot provide VAT evidence, we should hold payment and escalate — we can't accept unsupported zero-VAT invoices. Also check contract for any gross-up clause — we don't gross-up by default unless the SOW says so.

anna-accounting: I'll ask vendor to reissue with the explicit wording and attach the VIES screenshot. Also asking procurement to confirm whether contract has gross-up. Will pause payment until we have docs.

maria-fin: Sounds good. If vendor pushes for payment timing, we'll offer payment on receipt of compliant invoice + VIES screenshot. If they reissue without the wording, procurement/procurement@redwood will escalate.

tom-sales: FYI vendor asked for payment by EOM to lock in GBP rate — passing along.

anna-accounting: Added checklist in thread:
- Request VIES validation screenshot (supplier-provided)
- Ask vendor to reissue invoice with "reverse charge - VAT to be accounted for by recipient" wording or add VAT if they charge it
- Check contract for gross-up clause (procurement)
- Hold payment until docs are received

maria-fin: Thanks all. If we get the VIES screenshot, finance will process net amount and record reverse charge entries. If not, hold and tag @oliver-legal to advise next steps. :white_check_mark:

liam-ops: Noted — will use tax_code: RC_EU_EST when AP processes.

anna-accounting: Vendor replied: "We'll reissue tonight with reverse charge text and attach VAT certificate." I uploaded vendor message to ticket. Will update when invoice reissued. :+1:
